newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian diamond trade sees record turnover for '96.
newsitem.headline: Belgian diamond trade sees record turnover for '96.

text.p: Belgium's diamond trade, the world's biggest, is expecting a record turnover in 1996, the Diamond High Council (DHC) said on Friday.

It said in a statement on a recent meeting with a delegation from the De Beers Central Selling Organisation (CSO) that "in terms of manufacturing and trading Antwerp has had an encouraging year and turnover is expected to achieve a new record."
In 1995, total turnover in value terms of the diamond business, which is concentrated in the northern port of Antwerp, jumped to $21 billion from $18.5 billion in 1994.

The DHC said in the statement however that the momentum of the first half of the year had been difficult to sustain into the second half, following the mid-year price increase of rough gems and an erosion of profit margins.
The DHC said in October that total turnover in the first nine months of 1996 had risen 11 percent to $17.15 billion.
